back: People of working age who are without work, available for work and actively seeking work.
Everyone employed plus everyone unemployed (working or willing, able and seeking to work).
Everyone willing and able to work at the going wage has a job, apart from a small amount of frictional and seasonal unemployment.
People of working age neither working nor seeking work: students, homemakers, the retired, the long-term sick, discouraged workers.
A survey of a sample of households that classifies each person as employed, unemployed or inactive using international definitions.

front: Give two weaknesses of a labour force survey.
back: Costly and slow; sampling error; hides underemployment and discouraged workers; relies on honest answers.
Having some work but fewer hours than wanted, or work well below one's skills.

front: Can the number unemployed rise while the unemployment rate falls?
back: Yes: if the labour force grows by a larger percentage than the number unemployed.
